summary: CFB here means change from baseline in a roxadustat anaemia trial, not complement factor B.

quote: Importantly, during sepsis, absence of cfB conferred a protective effect with improved survival and cardiac function and markedly attenuated acute kidney injury.
summary: In mouse sepsis, cfB deletion improved survival and organ injury and reduced cytokine production, so cfB drives inflammatory injury (not a colitis model).

quote: Genome-wide association scan in north Indians reveals three novel HLA-independent risk loci for ulcerative colitis.
summary: A north Indian UC GWAS found an HLA-independent SNP signal at the CFB locus among novel risk loci, with no direction stated.

quote: Remarkably, six of the 17 genes concerned also harbor monoallelic (STAT3), biallelic (C3, CFB, CARD11, PIK3R1) or both monoallelic and biallelic (STAT1) LOF alleles in patients with other clinical phenotypes.
summary: CFB is only named in a list of genes with both gain- and loss-of-function alleles in a review of dominant immunodeficiencies; nothing on UC.

quote: Pathogenic complement gene mutations were found in 7 out of 8 patients tested (C3, MCP, or MCP combined with CFB or clusterin).
summary: CFB mutations appear within a list of complement gene mutations in influenza-associated thrombotic microangiopathy cases; unrelated to UC.
CFb denotes cardiac fibroblasts in a paper on ECM1 in the ageing heart, not complement factor B.

quote: In inflamed versus normal colonic mucosa of ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease, CFB mRNA was the most significantly overexpressed gene and the mRNA abundance ratio was among the 50 highest.
summary: CFB mRNA is the most overexpressed gene in inflamed UC and Crohn's colonic mucosa, made mainly by epithelial cells and induced by TLR3, with systemic complement activation in active IBD.

quote: Our study identified one risk locus (CFB) shared by IgAN and IBD, and genetic variants of CFB may affect complement activation and associate with the predisposition to IgAN.
summary: The IBD-associated CFB SNP rs4151657 is also associated with IgA nephropathy and with higher serum CFB and C3a levels; the study is in IgAN, not UC.

quote: Fourteen consecutive aHUS patients were screened for mutations in C3, CD46, CFH, CFI, and CFB, as well as factor H (FH) antibodies.
summary: CFB is one of several complement genes screened for mutations in atypical haemolytic uremic syndrome; no UC or CFB-specific result.

quote: Univariate Cox analysis and LASSO-Cox regression analysis were performed, and four genes (SPP1, DHRS3, SLC11A1, and CFB) with significant differential expression were selected through GEPIA.
summary: CFB is one of four genes in a prognostic risk-score model for thyroid cancer survival; not related to UC.

quote: Recombinant S252 CFB had reduced binding to C3b, its cleavage was impaired, and complement-driven phagocytosis and cytokine secretion were reduced compared with G252 CFB.
summary: A CFB coding variant (G252S) associated with perianal Crohn's disease is loss-of-function, impairing cleavage, complement activation and phagocytosis, implying CFB function is protective.

quote: Six sEV proteins were identified, namely, GCLM, KEL, APOF, CFB, PDE5A, and ATIC, which properly distinguished normal control, early neoplasia, and advanced neoplasia patients from each other.
summary: CFB in serum extracellular vesicles is part of a six-protein panel for detecting colorectal neoplasia; not about UC.
CFB means change from baseline in a vutrisiran amyloidosis quality-of-life study, not complement factor B.

quote: Gene-based low-frequency variants analysis suggests CFB as another potential susceptibility gene.
summary: An exome chip study in Han Chinese suggests CFB as a possible susceptibility gene for IgA nephropathy; not UC.

quote: One is in the complement component 2 gene (C2; E318D) and the other is in the complement factor B gene (CFB; R32Q).
summary: The CFB R32Q variant has a derived allele protective against age-related macular degeneration, flagged as a candidate protective variant; UC is not studied for CFB.

quote: Collectively, the present results suggested that CFB expression was an independent predictor of overall and disease-free survival in patients with LUAD.
summary: Low CFB expression predicts poorer survival in lung adenocarcinoma; not UC.

quote: Of the 28 CFB SNPs, similar strength of association was observed for rs4151657 (novel ulcerative colitis GWAS SNP) in north Indians (P=1.73 × 10-10) and Japanese (P=2.02 × 10-12) but not in the Dutch.
summary: CFB SNP rs4151657 is associated with UC in north Indian and Japanese cohorts but not Dutch, showing allelic heterogeneity across ethnic groups.

quote: Furthermore, EE suppressed the expression of C3aR, CFB, CD55, TLR4 and NLRP3.
summary: In TNBS colitis rats, Echinacea extract treatment lowered colonic CFB expression along with C3aR and other markers; CFB itself was not perturbed.
cfb here is a Staphylococcus aureus virulence gene, not human or mouse complement factor B.
The bfd match is a funder name (bfd Buchholz-Fachinformationsdienst) in an epigenetic clock paper, not the gene.

quote: CFD, F2RL2, CFB, C4BPA, F7, C4BPB, CFH, C3 and PROS1, which regulate the complement activation involved in inflammatory and immune responses.
summary: CFB is one of several complement genes downregulated by cordycepin or Cordyceps extract in LPS-challenged piglet intestine; no gene-specific result.

quote: Classically activated or M1 macrophages, which are pro-inflammatory and polarized by lipopolysaccharide (LPS) either alone or in association with Th1 cytokines such as IFN-γ, GM-CSF, and produce pro-inflammatory cytokines such as interleukin-1β (IL-1β), IL-6, IL-12, IL-23, and TNF-α; and 2) Alternatively activated or M2 macrophages, which are anti-inflammatory and immunoregulatory and polarized by Th2 cytokines such as IL-4 and IL-13 and produce anti-inflammatory cytokines such as IL-10 and TGF-β.
summary: GM-CSF is only named as one Th1 cytokine that polarizes M1 macrophages in a general macrophage review.

quote: Here we found that IL-23 induced production of the cytokine granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) in T(H)17 cells and that GM-CSF had an essential role in their encephalitogenicity.
summary: GM-CSF from IL-23-driven Th17 cells is essential for their pathogenicity in autoimmune neuroinflammation, so it promotes autoimmune inflammation (not a colitis model).

quote: The coordinate expression of IL-8, MCP-1, GM-CSF and TNF alpha appears to be a general property of human colon epithelial cells since an identical array of cytokines, as well as IL-6, also was expressed by freshly isolated human colon epithelial cells.
summary: Human colon epithelial cells upregulate GM-CSF mRNA and secretion when infected with invasive bacteria or stimulated with TNF or IL-1.

quote: Here, we show that deficient granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) production altered mononuclear phagocyte effector functions and led to reduced regulatory T cell (T(reg)) numbers and impaired oral tolerance.
summary: In mice, deficient GM-CSF, mainly from ILC3s, reduced Treg numbers and impaired oral tolerance, indicating GM-CSF supports intestinal homeostasis.
